title: HiLight on Pixel 11 Pro phones now supports Google Messages
summary: Google Messages joins the (still very small) official list of apps supporting HiLight.
body: TL;DR Google introduced its HiLight notification light with Pixel 11 Pro models this year. So far, HiLight has officially supported Phone and WhatsApp calls, as well as Gemini interactions. That’s now expanding to also include Google Messages. Google brought Pixel phones a new hardware feature this year, marking the debut of the HiLight notification light on Pixel 11 models, and now, with the release of the November Pixel Drop, it’s picking up some new functionality. Notification lights have been around since phones weren’t even that smart, but in recent years we’ve seen less and less of them — which is a shame, because they can be genuinely useful. But while we were excited to see Google embrace them again for Pixel 11 phones (well, the Pro models, anyway), so far HiLight has been a little limited in terms of what it can officially do.

title: Google rolls out Create My Widget to Pixel 10 and 11 series, but the Pixel 10a misses out
summary: You can now use natural language commands to generate widgets, but not on the budget Pixel.
body: Credit: Play Store TL;DR Google is rolling out the Create My Widget generative AI tool to Pixel 10 and Pixel 11 series via the November 2026 Pixel Feature Drop. The feature generates Material-style home screen widgets from natural-language text prompts, but notably excludes the Pixel 10a. Google confirmed that Create My Widget is also coming soon to the Pixel Watch 4 and Pixel Watch 5 in select regions. Google’s November 2026 Pixel Feature Drop is officially here, bringing one of the most anticipated personalization tools to your Pixel: Create My Widget. Google announced Create My Widget earlier this year, and is now formally rolling out the generative AI tool to help users design personalized home screen widgets tailored to their everyday needs and workflow. Until now, Create My Widget was surprisingly exclusive to Googlebook laptops , remaining conspicuously absent on Android/Pixel despite a brief sighting through a Google Play Store listing . With the November 2026 Pixel Feature Drop update, rolling out starting today, Pixel users can finally build their own widgets by choosing from curated suggestions or typing simple natural-language prompts.

title: Google’s beefing up Calculator with Pixel Solver and Unit Conversion tools
summary: How many rods to the hogshead does your car get?
body: TL;DR Google’s got a couple upgrades landing for Calculator as part of today’s November Feature Drop. Pixel Solver on Pixel 11 phones uses AI and templates to guide you through math problems. Unit Conversion aims to free you from constantly looking up formulas, and even supports monetary exchange rates. Google’s November Pixel Drop starts going out today, and in addition to seeing the expansion of features like Gboard’s Rambler and Gemini Intelligence , we’re also getting some brand-new ones — including a couple designed to offer a little math assistance: Pixel Solver and Unit Conversion for Google Calculator. We live in a world full of all different kinds of ways to measure things, and converting between them all can sometimes be less intuitive than we’d like — how often have you asked Gemini or Assistant in the kitchen to remind you how many cups are in a quart? While that’s still going to be an option, Google’s now bringing a more manual version of that to its Calculator app .

title: After months of waiting, you can finally buy a Pixel Tag
summary: You can finally buy Google's first tracker tag.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Google’s Pixel Tag is finally on sale today (November 11), months after the accessory was first unveiled. The tracker uses the Find Hub network, has an IP67 rating, and delivers precision finding via UWB and Bluetooth Channel Sounding. The Pixel Tag costs $29, although you can also buy a four-pack for $99. Google unveiled the Pixel Tag way back in August alongside the Pixel 11 range. However, the company’s tracker wasn’t actually available to purchase at the time. Thankfully, that changes today as the Pixel Tag is finally on sale. Google’s first tag (unsurprisingly) uses the Find Hub crowdsourced network of Android devices for location tracking. The Pixel Tag also brings an IP67 rating for dust and water resistance, UWB and Bluetooth Channel Sounding for more precise tracking, and a replaceable CR2032 battery that supposedly lasts for over a year.

title: Pixel’s Transit Mode is now automatic, and your daily commutes just got easier
summary: Google has announced Transit Mode 2.0, finally removing its biggest limitation.
body: TL;DR Google has announced Transit Mode 2.0 with the November Pixel Drop. It can now trigger automatically based on data from your phone’s sensors. It’s available on Pixel 6a and newer phones in all regions and languages. Google introduced Transit Mode on Pixel phones in April this year, and it’s been a handy addition for people who commute on public transport like trains and buses. However, it had one major flaw: you had to manually turn it on every time. If that bothered you as much as it did us, there’s some good news. Google has released the November Pixel Drop with custom icon styles, expanded HiLight support , and more. Among the plethora of updates is Transit Mode 2.0, which can now turn on automatically. Your Pixel phone can use data from its sensors to detect when you’re commuting and activate Transit Mode automatically. This finally brings the feature in line with Pixel’s Driving Mode and Bedtime Mode, which can already activate on their own.

body: TL;DR Google’s November Pixel Drop brings Gemini Intelligence to the Pixel 10 series, including Rambler, personalized suggestions, and expanded automations. Rambler cleans up voice dictation, while Gemini can now handle more multi-step tasks like ordering groceries, booking rides, and making restaurant reservations. Proactive Gemini Actions adds contextual text summaries, Google Keep grocery list integration, and wider global availability. Ever tried dictating a message, only to spend the next minute deleting all the “ums,” fixing awkward sentences, and wondering whether typing would’ve been faster? Or wished you could simply tell your phone to sort out dinner instead of hopping between apps? Google wants Gemini to take both headaches off your hands, and its latest Pixel Drop is bringing more of that convenience to older Pixel phones. The November Pixel Drop is rolling out today, bringing Gemini Intelligence to the Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro, Pixel 10 Pro XL, and Pixel 10 Pro Fold. The expansion brings several capabilities already available on the Pixel 11 series to Google’s previous-generation flagships, including Rambler , personalized suggestions, and expanded automation features.

title: A Google TV Ambient Mode issue is causing repetitive photo slideshows and frozen screens
summary: Rolling back recent updates appears to fix the problem.
body: TL;DR Some Google TV owners are experiencing repetitive Google Photos slideshows and freezing in Ambient Mode. The problem affects Chromecast with Google TV and Google TV Streamer devices, although it doesn’t appear to affect everyone. Uninstalling Ambient Mode updates restores normal photo slideshows for some affected devices. Google TV can turn your idle screen into a digital photo frame, bringing your favorite memories to the biggest screen in the house. Google even spruced up the experience earlier this year with dynamic slideshows that transform ordinary photos into colorful collages. But for some users, that personal touch has become a frustrating exercise in repetition, with Ambient Mode recycling the same handful of pictures before freezing altogether.
